# Nazar

> Nazar ("Har batch par nazar", an eye on every batch) checks any Indian medicine batch number against alerts published by CDSCO, state drug regulators and WHO, and answers with exactly one of four states: Flagged, Retracted, No alert found, or Can't tell. It never says a medicine is "safe"; "No alert found" is not a safety certificate. Every alert is a public, readonly entity on the Arkiv Tiramisu testnet, created by one publisher wallet, so anyone can verify it without trusting Nazar. Built for the Arkiv Global Tour, Best Indian Use Case track.

## Live

- [Web app](https://nazar-nu.vercel.app): check a batch, alerts, cabinet, shelf sweep, Arkiv directory, AI assistant guide
- [REST API](https://nazar-api-production.up.railway.app/health): base URL https://nazar-api-production.up.railway.app, e.g. GET /v1/check?batch=SR-13
- [MCP server](https://nazar-nu.vercel.app/ai): https://nazar-api-production.up.railway.app/mcp, stateless Streamable HTTP, read-only, no key
- [Publisher on the Arkiv explorer](https://tiramisu.explorer.arkiv.network/address/0xd06d85Eb20f126f796E4a341b711B1a757c66bD2): 0xd06d85Eb20f126f796E4a341b711B1a757c66bD2, project tag "nazar-in-batch-alerts"
- [Alerts RSS feed](https://nazar-api-production.up.railway.app/v1/alerts.rss): also .atom and .json
